function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

message.content: Pizza’s roots trace back to ancient Mediterranean flatbreads—think Greek *plakous* or Roman *panis focacius*. However, the modern version we know today began in Naples, Italy, around the late 18th‑early 19th century. Neapolitan cooks started topping simple yeast dough with tomatoes (introduced to Europe only after the Columbian Exchange), garlic, olive oil, oregano, and fresh mozzarella made from cow's milk. These “pizza Margherita” slices were named after Queen Margherita of Savoy when she visited Naples; her favorite toppings—red tomato, white cheese, and green basil—mirrored the Italian flag colors. From there, pizza spread across Italy and eventually worldwide, evolving into countless regional styles.
